name: Health & medicine
characteristic: which function of the health enterprise the field carries out: treat an individual patient, protect a population, develop a therapy, engineer a device or a beam, run and inform the system, train its workforce
positive_test: the work serves human health and its success is judged by a clinical, epidemiological or health-system outcome
negative_test: biology studied for its own sake (Life sciences); the brain studied as an organ of cognition (Neuroscience); a demand made on the model such as fairness on clinical data (Desired properties); the imaging or signal type alone (Modality)
notes: Largest branch. 38 names / 134 mentions are branch-level surfaces that name no depth-2 child (Medical Imaging 48, Healthcare 16, Biomedical*, AI in Healthcare) and stay at depth 1, per the Bioinformatics ruling in AXES.md 7.

name: Clinical medicine
characteristic: which organ system, patient population or disease the specialty treats
positive_test: names a medical specialty, a disease or a patient population whose care supplies the problem
negative_test: the disease mechanism studied molecularly with no clinical intent (Life sciences); the drug itself (Pharmacology); a diagnostic model property (Desired properties)
examples: Oncology; Psychiatry & mental health; Paediatrics
notes: Absorbs disorder-named research (Autism Research 8, Neurodegenerative Diseases 3, Psychiatric Genetics) under the declared rule: a disorder studied to care for patients is Health, a brain studied to learn how brains work is Neuroscience. Radiology sits here as a depth-3; Medical Imaging 48 does NOT, it is a branch-level surface.

name: Medical physics
characteristic: which physical agent is delivered to or measured in the patient
positive_test: the problem is the physics of a therapeutic or diagnostic beam, dose or tracer
negative_test: image analysis with no physical-delivery question (Modality > Vision + Clinical medicine); device electronics (Biomedical engineering)
examples: Radiation therapy planning; Dosimetry; Nuclear medicine physics
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (medical physics 18). Brachytherapy 8, radiation oncology 5, radiotherapy 3 cluster here; an unusually strong local cluster from one collaboration, kept because medical physics is a standing profession (AAPM), not an artefact of 2024.

name: Public health
characteristic: which population-level determinant of health the field acts on
positive_test: the unit of concern is a population, not a patient
negative_test: care of individuals (Clinical medicine); organisation and financing of care (Health services research); climate or pollution studied as environmental science (Physical & environmental)
examples: Epidemiology; Global health; Disease surveillance
notes: Epidemiology 20 is filed as a depth-3 child rather than a sibling: it is the basic science of public health. Naming the node Epidemiology would have excluded global health and surveillance.

name: Health services research
characteristic: which part of the delivery system is being measured or improved: policy, financing, access, or the patient's experience of care
positive_test: the object of study is how care is organised, paid for, reached or experienced
negative_test: the clinical decision itself (Clinical medicine); the information system (Health informatics); economics as a discipline (Social & behavioural > Economics)
examples: Health policy; Healthcare access & equity; Patient-centred care
notes: Holds Health Economics 3, against AXES.md 7 which files it under Social & behavioural sciences; see RATIONALE defect D3. Shared Decision Making 5 lands here and is the clinical homonym that broke v0's `decision making` node.

name: Health informatics
characteristic: which layer of clinical information is handled: the record, the decision support, or the remote channel
positive_test: the problem is representing, moving or acting on clinical data as an information system
negative_test: the statistical model of a disease (Clinical medicine); generic data engineering (uninformative); the imaging data type (Modality)
examples: Clinical decision support; Electronic health records; Telemedicine & mHealth
notes: Scopus ASJC 2718 Health Informatics. Digital Health 6, Health Informatics 8, Telemedicine 3.

name: Medical education
characteristic: who is being trained and by what means
positive_test: the learner is a clinician or clinician-in-training and the claim is about their competence
negative_test: education in general (Social & behavioural > Education); patient education (Health services research); evaluation of a model (mark_ignore)
examples: Surgical simulation training; Clinical skills assessment; Clinician AI literacy
notes: Filed under Health rather than Education because the field is owned by health faculties and its outcome is clinical competence; a re-extraction that adds nursing or allied-health education lands here too.

name: Pharmacology
characteristic: which stage of the therapeutic pipeline the work serves: discovery, response prediction, or safety
positive_test: the object is a drug, a vaccine or a therapeutic agent and its effect on an organism
negative_test: the molecule as a chemical object with no therapeutic claim (Physical & environmental > Chemistry); the immune mechanism itself (Life sciences > Immunology & microbiology)
examples: Drug discovery; Pharmacogenomics; Toxicology
notes: OECD FOS 3.1 places pharmacology and pharmacy in medical sciences. Drug Discovery 7 is the anchor; the molecular-representation half of those same papers maps to Modality > Molecular and often to Chemistry.

name: Biomedical engineering
characteristic: which physical interface to the body is engineered: a device, a neural interface, or a rehabilitation aid
positive_test: the deliverable is a physical or signal-processing artefact that touches a patient
negative_test: the physics of a radiation beam (Medical physics); the neuroscience question the interface is used to answer (Neuroscience); robot autonomy as such (Robotics)
examples: Medical devices; Brain-computer interfaces; Rehabilitation engineering
notes: OECD FOS 2.6 Medical engineering. Filed under Health rather than Computing because the outcome is clinical. Brain-computer interfaces are the contested member: the interface is engineering, the decoding question is Neuroscience.

name: Neuroscience & cognitive science
characteristic: at what level of organisation the nervous system or the mind is being explained: cell, circuit, whole-brain cognition, formal model, or mind-as-such
positive_test: the brain or the mind is the object of study and the claim is about how it works
negative_test: a brain disorder studied in order to treat patients (Health > Clinical medicine); brain-inspired machinery proposed to improve AI (Method > Model design); behaviour of persons and groups (Social & behavioural > Psychology)
notes: Compound L1 name that no listed classification system reproduces: OECD FOS 5.1 groups cognitive science with psychology, Scopus splits Cognitive Neuroscience (2805) from Experimental & Cognitive Psychology (3205). Kept because L1 is locked; see RATIONALE defect D4. 21 names / 147 mentions are branch-level surfaces (Neuroscience 84, Neuroimaging 28, fMRI/MRI names) that reach no depth-2 child.

name: Cognitive neuroscience
characteristic: which cognitive function is being mapped to brain activity
positive_test: a named cognitive function (memory, attention, language, social cognition) is related to measured brain activity
negative_test: the cognitive function modelled without brain measurement (Cognitive science); circuit mechanism with no cognitive claim (Systems neuroscience); clinical diagnosis (Health)
examples: Memory & attention; Brain decoding of stimuli; Social cognition
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (cognitive neuroscience 13). Brain Decoding/Encoding and naturalistic-stimulus work sit here; the fMRI surface itself is Modality > Vision.

name: Systems neuroscience
characteristic: which circuit or system of the brain produces the measured signal: connectivity, sensory pathway, or motor output
positive_test: the object is a neural circuit, population or pathway and its dynamics
negative_test: the cognitive interpretation of that activity (Cognitive neuroscience); a model formalism proposed as theory (Computational neuroscience)
examples: Neural circuits & dynamics; Sensory systems; Motor control
notes: Scopus ASJC 2801/2809. Absorbs connectomics, functional connectivity 4, electrophysiology 3 and the sensory-systems cluster (Vision Science 2, Visual Neuroscience, Sensory Systems), which Scopus lists separately; merged here to keep the branch at five children, split when sensory work grows.

name: Cellular & molecular neuroscience
characteristic: which subcellular or developmental mechanism of the nervous system is studied
positive_test: the object is a neuron, a synapse or a developmental process at cell or molecule scale
negative_test: circuit-level dynamics (Systems neuroscience); genetics of a disorder (Health or Life sciences)
examples: Synaptic plasticity; Neurodevelopment; Neuronal morphology
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept. Scopus ASJC 2804 and 2806. Two corpus names only: this institute does no wet-lab neuroscience in 2024, which is a finding about the institute, not evidence the category is wrong; a 2023-2026 re-extraction with one new collaboration fills it.

name: Computational neuroscience
characteristic: which formal account of neural computation is proposed or tested
positive_test: the contribution is a model or theory whose claim is that the brain computes this way
negative_test: using any model as a tool to analyse brain data (the phenomenon's node); proposing brain-like machinery to improve AI (Method > Model design & analysis)
examples: Spiking network models; Normative theories of neural coding; Deep networks as models of cortex
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (computational neuroscience 16). The negative test is load-bearing: almost every paper in this branch is computational, so without it this node absorbs the branch. Neuromorphic and neuroscience-inspired-AI names are routed OUT to Method; see RATIONALE rejections.

name: Cognitive science
characteristic: which faculty of mind is modelled independently of its neural substrate
positive_test: the claim is about how minds represent or reason, with no brain measurement required
negative_test: measured brain activity (Cognitive neuroscience); behaviour of persons and groups (Social & behavioural > Psychology); reasoning demanded of a model (Task)
examples: Cognitive modelling; Theory of mind; Concept learning in humans
notes: The boundary with Social & behavioural > Psychology is declared, not discovered: mechanisms of cognition here, behaviour of persons and groups there. OECD FOS 5.1 would put both in the social sciences; see defect D4.

name: Life sciences
characteristic: which level of the living world the field studies: genome, molecule and cell, organism and population, host and pathogen, or cultivated plant
positive_test: a living system supplies the problem and the claim is biological
negative_test: the biology is being acted on to treat a patient (Health); the sequence or structure as a data type (Modality > Molecular & biological data); the organism is a brain (Neuroscience)
notes: 13 names / 85 mentions are branch-level surfaces, chiefly Bioinformatics 40 and Computational Biology 33, exactly as AXES.md 7 rules. That means a third of this branch never reaches depth 2.

name: Genetics & genomics
characteristic: which scale of the genome is interrogated: variant, regulation, expression, or population
positive_test: the object is heritable sequence and what it determines
negative_test: the sequence treated purely as a string to model (Modality > Molecular); a genetic finding used for patient care (Health > Clinical medicine)
examples: Functional genomics; Population genetics; Single-cell transcriptomics
notes: AXES.md 7 lists `genomics` and `genetics` as two children; merged here because genome-scale vs heredity is a granularity difference, not a division principle, and OECD FOS 1.6 / Scopus ASJC 1311 carry one field. The fused display name is the established one (NHGRI, journals); see RATIONALE.

name: Molecular & cell biology
characteristic: which molecular machine or cellular process is characterised
positive_test: the object is a protein, a pathway or a cell and how it works
negative_test: the protein as a sequence or graph to be modelled (Modality); a drug candidate (Health > Pharmacology); the immune system specifically (Immunology & microbiology)
examples: Structural biology; Proteomics; Systems biology
notes: Renames AXES.md 7's `molecular & structural biology`, which fuses two levels; structural biology becomes a depth-3 child. Established department name (MCB); OECD FOS 1.6 Biochemistry & molecular biology + Cell biology.

name: Ecology & evolution
characteristic: which scale of organism-environment relation is studied: species, community, or lineage over time
positive_test: the object is organisms in their environment or their evolutionary history
negative_test: the physical environment itself (Physical & environmental > Earth & environmental sciences); agriculture as production (Agricultural & plant sciences); satellite imagery as data (Modality)
examples: Biodiversity & conservation; Species distribution modelling; Phylogenetics
notes: Fused name taken directly from Scopus ASJC 1105 `Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics`, so the compound is the established field name and not an invented pair. Absorbs the conservation cluster (conservation biology 4, biodiversity monitoring, species distribution modelling 5).

name: Immunology & microbiology
characteristic: which side of the host-pathogen relation is studied
positive_test: the object is an immune system, a microbe or a virus
negative_test: vaccination or immunotherapy as a treatment (Health > Pharmacology); epidemic spread in a population (Health > Public health)
examples: Immune repertoire analysis; Viral genomics; Host-pathogen interaction
notes: Fused name taken from Scopus ASJC 2400. Forced in part by AXES.md 7 (immunology 9). Microbiology is near-absent in 2024 and is kept as a blind spot.

name: Agricultural & plant sciences
characteristic: which agricultural resource is measured or managed: crop, soil, or forest
positive_test: the object is a cultivated or managed biological resource
negative_test: wild ecosystems (Ecology & evolution); the agri-food business (Industry & commerce, currently with no node); land cover as imagery (Modality)
examples: Crop phenotyping; Soil science; Forestry
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept. OECD FOS 4 makes agricultural sciences a top-level field, and AXES.md's eight branches have no home for it; filed here as a science rather than in Industry as a sector. See defect D6 for the seam this creates.

name: Computing & software systems
characteristic: which ACM CCS top-level area of computing supplies the problem
positive_test: an artefact of computing - a program, a system, a network, an interface, a rendered image, a proof - is what the work builds, analyses or secures
negative_test: the artefact is the learning machinery itself (Method); a property demanded of a model (Desired properties); AI's own subfields such as Multi-Agent Systems or Embodied AI (not an application domain)
notes: Children follow ACM CCS 2012 top-level areas. The branch is large because software engineering 36 and HCI 27 are two of the institute's real collaborations, not because the node is loose.

name: Software engineering
characteristic: which phase of the software lifecycle is served: construction, testing, maintenance, or the language and tooling it is written in
positive_test: the object is source code, a software process or a development artefact
negative_test: code generation judged as an output type (Task > Generation); a proof obligation (Theory of computation); the runtime system that executes it (Computer systems & architecture)
examples: Software testing & verification; Programming languages & compilers; Empirical software engineering
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (software engineering 36). ACM CCS `Software and its engineering`, which is also where programming languages and compilers sit, so they are depth-3 here rather than a sibling. MLOps and `Software Engineering for Machine Learning` are kept here: the served field is software engineering, which exists without AI.

name: Human-centered computing
characteristic: which aspect of the human-computer relation is designed or measured: interface, accessibility, collaboration, or immersion
positive_test: the object is a person's interaction with a computing system
negative_test: the robot as a physical agent (Robotics > Human-robot interaction); psychology of the person independent of a system (Social & behavioural > Psychology); interpretability demanded of a model (Desired properties)
examples: Interaction design & usability; Accessibility; Mixed reality
notes: Name taken verbatim from ACM CCS. Forced by AXES.md 7 (HCI 27). Visualization is a depth-3 child here, per CCS, not under Computer graphics.

name: Computer graphics
characteristic: which step of synthesising or processing visual geometry is addressed: rendering, geometry, or motion
positive_test: the deliverable is synthesised or processed geometry, light or motion
negative_test: recognising content in an image (Modality > Vision + Task); image generation judged as an output (Task > Generation); visualization of data (Human-centered computing)
examples: Rendering; Geometry processing; Character animation
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (graphics 9). ACM CCS `Computing methodologies > Computer graphics`. The 3D cluster (3D reconstruction, meshes, point clouds) splits: the data type to Modality, the synthesis question here.

name: Computer networks
characteristic: which layer of networked communication is engineered: protocol, routing, or the physical link
positive_test: the object is how machines communicate and the claim is about the network
negative_test: operating a commercial telecom network (Industry > Telecommunications); distributed training of a model (Method > Training regime); network as a mathematical object (Modality > Graphs)
examples: Network protocols & routing; Wireless & mobile networks; Internet of Things
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (networks). Declared homonym with Industry > Telecommunications: networking research here, running a carrier's network there. `Network Science` and `Network Design` are NOT here - they are graph machinery.

name: Computer security
characteristic: which attack surface of a deployed system is defended: code, network, or data
positive_test: the adversary attacks a computing system and the field of computer security supplies the problem
negative_test: an adversary attacking the model itself - adversarial examples, membership inference, poisoning (Desired properties > Trustworthy AI); privacy as a demand on learning (Desired properties)
examples: Vulnerability detection; Malware & intrusion detection; Digital forensics
notes: Deliberately NOT named `Security & privacy` (the ACM CCS name): that name would attract the ~40 mentions of privacy-of-ML and adversarial-robustness work that AXES.md 2 assigns to Desired properties. See defect D13.

name: Computer systems & architecture
characteristic: which layer of the machine is designed or scheduled: the distributed system, the processor, or the data store
positive_test: the object is the machine or the system that runs computations, and the claim is about its organisation
negative_test: making a model cheaper to run (Desired properties > Frugal AI, including Hardware Acceleration); distributed or federated training as a learning regime (Method); database content as tabular data (Modality)
examples: Distributed & parallel systems; Computer architecture & accelerators; Databases & data management
notes: Merges two ACM CCS top-levels (`Computer systems organization` and `Hardware`) because at 25 mentions no principle separates them in this corpus; split when EDA or chip-design work appears. Quantum computing is a depth-3 child here.

name: Theory of computation
characteristic: which formal object is reasoned about: an automaton, a logic, or an algorithm's cost
positive_test: the object is computation itself as a formal system, and the claim is a proof or a decision procedure
negative_test: theory of learning and generalization (Method > Learning theory); optimization or graph machinery used to solve a problem (Method > Inference & optimization); verifying a neural network (Method > Model design, per AXES.md 5)
examples: Automata & formal languages; Logic & automated theorem proving; Algorithms & complexity
notes: Judgement addition; ACM CCS `Theory of computation`. This is also where AI-for-mathematics would have to go today, which is a symptom of the missing mathematics branch (defect D5).

name: Physical & environmental sciences
characteristic: which natural system is explained or measured: matter at its smallest scale, chemical transformation, engineered material, the sky, the atmosphere, or the earth
positive_test: a non-living natural system supplies the problem
negative_test: the living system (Life sciences); physics used as an inductive bias for a model, e.g. physics-informed networks (Method > Model design); the sector that sells energy (Industry > Energy & utilities)
notes: Children follow OECD FOS 1.3-1.5 plus Scopus 2500 Materials Science. Remote Sensing 11 is a branch-level surface here (Modality > Vision + this branch), per the AXES.md 7 ruling.

name: Astronomy & astrophysics
characteristic: which scale of the universe is studied: object, galaxy, or cosmos
positive_test: the object of study is beyond the earth's atmosphere
negative_test: the telescope's data pipeline as image processing (Modality); particle physics done in a terrestrial detector (Physics)
examples: Cosmology; Galaxy formation & evolution; Survey & transient detection
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (astrophysics 15). Fused name is OECD FOS 1.3's own label `Astronomy (incl. astrophysics, space science)`.

name: Physics
characteristic: which physical regime supplies the problem: subatomic, quantum, or continuum
positive_test: the claim is about a physical system's behaviour and would be published in a physics venue
negative_test: physics-informed or physics-guided learning, where physics supplies the inductive bias and not the problem (Method); astronomy (Astronomy & astrophysics); materials as engineered artefacts (Materials science)
examples: Particle & high-energy physics; Quantum & condensed-matter physics; Computational physics
notes: Judgement addition; AXES.md 7 names no physics node although High Energy Physics 5, Particle Physics 2, Neutrino Physics 2 and Physics 5 are present. The negative test carries the load: a name as general as `Physics` would otherwise attract every physics-flavoured method name.

name: Chemistry
characteristic: which chemical question is asked: structure and energy, dynamics, or synthesis route
positive_test: the object is a molecule or reaction and the claim is chemical
negative_test: the molecule as a graph or sequence to model (Modality > Molecular); the molecule as a drug candidate (Health > Pharmacology); the bulk material (Materials science)
examples: Computational & quantum chemistry; Molecular simulation; Reaction & retrosynthesis prediction
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (computational chemistry 12). `Molecular Property Prediction` 7 and `Molecular Modeling` are declared cross-axis homonyms: chemistry, life sciences or pharmacology depending on the claim; the Modality value is the same in all three.

name: Materials science
characteristic: which stage of the materials cycle is served: discovery, characterisation, or processing
positive_test: the object is a bulk or nanoscale material and its properties in use
negative_test: the quantum-chemical calculation itself (Chemistry); the manufacturing line that uses the material (Industry > Manufacturing)
examples: Materials discovery; Interatomic potentials; Crystallography & characterisation
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (materials). Scopus ASJC 2500.

name: Climate science
characteristic: which part of the climate problem is addressed: the model, the forecast, or the impact
positive_test: the object is the climate or weather system, its simulation or its projected effects
negative_test: the carbon cost of training a model (Desired properties > Frugal AI); energy systems as a sector (Industry > Energy & utilities); environmental monitoring on the ground (Earth & environmental sciences)
examples: Climate modelling & emulation; Weather forecasting; Climate impact assessment
notes: Promoted from an OECD FOS 1.5 subfield (`Climatic research`) to depth 2 on semantics, not count: AI-for-climate is a standing worldwide application family that must survive a re-extraction. AXES.md 2 documents the Green-AI collision that this node must not absorb.

name: Earth & environmental sciences
characteristic: which earth compartment is monitored or modelled: solid earth, water, or the human environment
positive_test: the object is the earth system or the human environment and its state
negative_test: the climate system itself (Climate science); living communities in it (Life sciences > Ecology & evolution); satellite imagery as a data type (Modality)
examples: Environmental monitoring; Hydrology & water resources; Seismology & geospatial analysis
notes: Fused name is OECD FOS 1.5's own label, `Earth and related environmental sciences`, so it is not an invented pair. Holds the sustainability, pollution and disaster cluster.

name: Social & behavioural sciences
characteristic: which OECD FOS 5 discipline of human behaviour and institutions supplies the problem: mind, learning, markets, rules, society, or language
positive_test: the object is human behaviour, an institution or a human language, studied as a discipline
negative_test: the sector an institution operates in (Industry & commerce); the mind's mechanisms (Neuroscience & cognitive science); governance demanded of AI itself (Desired properties)
notes: Children follow OECD FOS 5 one-for-one, as AXES.md 7 and TAIL_VALIDATION F6 require after `Language, mind & behaviour` was withdrawn. The whole branch is 72 mentions: small, and that is a finding about a computing institute, not a defect.

name: Psychology
characteristic: which aspect of the person is studied: social behaviour, development over the lifespan, or clinical presentation
positive_test: the object is the behaviour or traits of persons and groups
negative_test: the mechanism of cognition (Neuroscience & cognitive science > Cognitive science); psychiatric care of patients (Health > Clinical medicine); a model's emotional-recognition output (Task)
examples: Social & personality psychology; Developmental psychology; Health psychology
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (psychology ~8), which cites LCC BF, Dewey 150 and OECD FOS 5.1 agreeing. The declared boundary with Cognitive science is the branch's weakest seam; see defect D4.

name: Education
characteristic: which part of the educational process is served: instruction, assessment, or the learner model
positive_test: the object is teaching or learning by humans in an educational setting
negative_test: training clinicians (Health > Medical education); machine learning that happens to be called learning (Method); an edtech company's product economics (Industry)
examples: Intelligent tutoring systems; Educational data mining; Assessment & feedback
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (education). OECD FOS 5.3.

name: Economics
characteristic: which economic object is modelled: agent behaviour, market mechanism, or econometric estimate
positive_test: the claim is economic and would be published in an economics venue
negative_test: a firm in a sector (Industry & commerce); game theory or mechanism design as machinery (Method > Inference & optimization); health economics, which serves the health system (Health > Health services research)
examples: Econometrics; Behavioural economics; Market & mechanism design
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (`economics-as-discipline`). The discipline/sector split is AXES.md's own and is the reason Finance sits in Industry.

name: Public policy & law
characteristic: which instrument of collective decision is studied: a public policy, a legal rule, or a public service
positive_test: the object is a government policy, a law or a public programme that exists independently of AI
negative_test: governance, regulation or accountability demanded of AI systems (Desired properties > Trustworthy AI); a policy in the reinforcement-learning sense (Method); health policy (Health > Health services research)
examples: Public policy analysis; Legal reasoning & regulation; Social services & welfare
notes: The node name deliberately avoids the bare word `Policy`: 11 corpus names contain `Policy` and 6 of them are reinforcement-learning policies (Policy Optimization 4, PPO, Policy Ensemble). This is TAIL_VALIDATION F7's homonym, measured; see defect D10. Merges OECD FOS 5.5 and 5.6, which are separately near-empty here, following ACM CCS `Law, social and behavioral sciences`.

name: Sociology
characteristic: which social aggregate is studied: an online public, a scientific community, or a demographic structure
positive_test: the object is collective human behaviour above the individual
negative_test: an individual's psychology (Psychology); a media company's product (Industry > Media & entertainment); misinformation detection as an output type (Task > Detection)
examples: Computational social science; Social media & online communities; Science & technology studies
notes: OECD FOS 5.4. BLIND SPOT: computational social science is a large ML application area worldwide and is nearly absent here (15 mentions), kept.

name: Linguistics
characteristic: which level of language structure is studied: sound and form, meaning, or use in context
positive_test: the object is human language as a system, and the claim is about language rather than about a model of it
negative_test: NLP engineering on text (Modality > Language & text); multilingual model building (Modality + Method); the language task itself (Task)
examples: Syntax & morphology; Semantics; Sociolinguistics & language variation
notes: CONTESTED placement, flagged by AXES.md 7 and TAIL_VALIDATION F6: OECD FOS 6.2 and LCC P file linguistics under Humanities, Scopus lists it under both Social Sciences and Arts & Humanities; filed here per the locked decision. The negative test is essential - most of the corpus's 26 mentions are one decision away from being mere Modality values.

name: Robotics & autonomous systems
characteristic: which capability of a physical autonomous agent the field is responsible for: acting on objects, moving through the world, driving, working with people, coordinating with other machines, or holding a plant on target
positive_test: a physical system must act in the world, and the field of robotics or control engineering supplies the problem
negative_test: control theory, optimal control and Lyapunov analysis as mathematical machinery (Method > Inference & optimization); reinforcement learning as the feedback signal (Method); continuous control as an output type (Task); the transport system the vehicle runs in (Industry)
notes: 7 names / 37 mentions are branch-level surfaces (Robotics 25, Robot Learning, Embodied AI 5) that reach no depth-2 child.

name: Robotic manipulation
characteristic: which stage of physical interaction with an object is solved: reaching, grasping, or in-hand control
positive_test: the robot must change the state of an object it touches
negative_test: moving the robot itself (Mobile robotics); the learning algorithm used to do it (Method); tactile data as a signal (Modality)
examples: Grasping; Dexterous in-hand manipulation; Assembly & insertion
notes: IEEE RAS subfield. Thin in this corpus (8 mentions) but one of the two canonical robot capability families; kept.

name: Mobile robotics
characteristic: how the robot establishes where it is and moves there: mapping, planning, or locomotion
positive_test: the robot's own position or motion through the environment is the problem
negative_test: driving a car on public roads (Autonomous vehicles); web or dialogue navigation, which is a metaphor (Task); path planning as combinatorial machinery (Method)
examples: SLAM & localisation; Motion planning; Legged locomotion
notes: Holds the navigation/SLAM/locomotion cluster. `Web Navigation` is explicitly excluded by the negative test - a name that would otherwise slip in on the word navigation.

name: Autonomous vehicles
characteristic: which part of the driving stack is addressed: perceiving the scene, predicting other agents, or planning the manoeuvre
positive_test: the system drives a vehicle on public roads among human traffic
negative_test: the transport network, fleet or timetable (Industry > Transportation & logistics); driving scenes as a vision dataset (Modality); trajectory prediction as an output type (Task)
examples: Driving scene perception; Pedestrian & agent trajectory prediction; Simulation & scenario generation
notes: Kept in Robotics rather than Industry because the research is perception-planning-control on a physical agent; the declared seam with Industry > Transportation & logistics is the vehicle vs the system it runs in.

name: Human-robot interaction
characteristic: in what relation the human stands to the robot: collaborator, bystander, or care recipient
positive_test: the presence of a human changes what the robot must do
negative_test: interaction with a screen or software interface (Computing > Human-centered computing); the human's psychology as such (Social & behavioural > Psychology)
examples: Collaborative robots; Socially aware navigation; Assistive & care robotics
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept: 3 mentions. HRI is a full field with its own conference (ACM/IEEE HRI); its near-absence is an accident of this year's collaborations.

name: Multi-robot systems
characteristic: what the fleet must share to act as one: perception, plan, or control authority
positive_test: two or more physical robots must coordinate
negative_test: multi-agent reinforcement learning or multi-agent systems as AI subfields, which fail `exists without AI` (Method); a single robot (the capability nodes)
examples: Swarm robotics; Collaborative mapping; Decentralised task allocation
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (multi-robot). The negative test keeps out MARL 14 and `Multi-Agent Systems` 11, which are the largest nearby corpus cluster and belong to Method.

name: Control systems engineering
characteristic: which physical plant is held on target: a vehicle, a process, or a networked system
positive_test: an engineered physical plant must be kept on a trajectory or setpoint, and the engineering of that controller is the problem
negative_test: control theory, optimal control, model predictive control and Lyapunov analysis when the contribution is the mathematics (Method > Inference & optimization); continuous-control benchmarks (Task)
examples: Process & industrial control; Flight & vehicle control; Networked and cyber-physical control
notes: CONTESTED. AXES.md 7 lists `control systems` 9 in this branch, but its own ruling that Game Theory and Operations Research are machinery sends control theory to Method. The split used here - the mathematics to Method, the engineered plant to Application - mirrors the Operational-Research-in-Public-Transportation resolution in TAIL_VALIDATION; it needs an owner decision (defect D2).

name: Industry & commerce
characteristic: which economic sector operates the system the work serves (children follow ISIC Rev.4 sections / GICS sectors)
positive_test: the beneficiary is an industry that would run this system with or without AI
negative_test: the discipline that studies that sector (Social & behavioural > Economics); operations research, routing and scheduling machinery (Method > Inference & optimization); the physical vehicle or robot (Robotics)
notes: AXES.md 7 names this branch twice and differently (`Industry & commerce` in the table, `Industry & economics` in the prose); the table's name is used. Smallest branch at 89 mentions. Do not read that as a defect to fix: it measures how little of a public research institute's 2024 output is sector-facing.

name: Energy & utilities
characteristic: which part of the energy chain is operated: generation, grid, storage, or demand
positive_test: the work serves the production, distribution or consumption of energy as an operated system
negative_test: the energy or carbon cost of training models (Desired properties > Frugal AI); climate science (Physical & environmental > Climate science); building design (Built environment)
examples: Power grid operation; Renewable generation forecasting; Demand response & storage
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (energy sector) and by its Green-AI collision argument in 2, which this node is the application half of.

name: Transportation & logistics
characteristic: which flow is scheduled or routed: people, freight, or fleet resources
positive_test: the work serves moving people or goods through a transport or supply system
negative_test: the vehicle's own autonomy (Robotics > Autonomous vehicles); vehicle routing, TSP or scheduling as combinatorial machinery (Method); traffic as a time series (Modality)
examples: Public transport planning; Freight & supply chain; Traffic management
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (transportation, supply chain). This is the sector in TAIL_VALIDATION's validated example `Operational Research in Public Transportation` = Method + this node.

name: Manufacturing
characteristic: which stage of production is served: process control, scheduling, or quality
positive_test: the work serves making physical goods at industrial scale
negative_test: job-shop scheduling as a combinatorial problem class (Method); materials themselves (Physical & environmental > Materials science); the plant's controller as engineering (Robotics > Control systems engineering)
examples: Process optimisation; Production scheduling; Quality inspection & predictive maintenance
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (manufacturing). BLIND SPOT at 5 mentions: industrial ML is one of the largest application sectors globally.

name: Finance & insurance
characteristic: which financial activity is served: allocation, risk, or transaction integrity
positive_test: the work serves a financial or insurance operation
negative_test: economics as a discipline (Social & behavioural > Economics); portfolio optimisation as convex machinery (Method); fraud detection as an output type (Task > Detection)
examples: Portfolio & asset allocation; Credit & insurance risk; Fraud & AML monitoring
notes: Forced by AXES.md 7 (finance-as-sector). ISIC K. BLIND SPOT at 3 mentions: kept because finance is among the two or three largest industrial users of ML.

name: Built environment
characteristic: which scale of constructed space is modelled: the building, the city, or the construction process
positive_test: the object is constructed physical space and its operation
negative_test: energy generation and grids (Energy & utilities); urban populations as a social object (Social & behavioural > Sociology); indoor positioning for a robot (Robotics > Mobile robotics)
examples: Building energy modelling; Urban planning & mobility; Construction & BIM
notes: Judgement addition (ISIC F + urban planning). The corpus cluster is real (Data-driven Building Models 3, smart buildings, urban planning) and had no home among AXES.md 7's named sectors.

name: Media & entertainment
characteristic: which media product is produced or operated: a game, a content platform, or creative work
positive_test: the work serves producing or operating entertainment or media content as a business
negative_test: games used as reinforcement-learning benchmarks, e.g. StarCraft (not an application domain); recommendation as an output type (Task > Recommendation); generation of images, music or video as an output type (Task)
examples: Game development & testing; Content platforms & moderation; Creative production tools
notes: Judgement addition (GICS Media & Entertainment). Declared homonym: `Game Playing`, `StarCraft II Micro-Management` are benchmarks, while `Game Development`, `Automated Game Testing`, `Toxicity Detection in Online Gaming` serve the games industry.

name: Retail & consumer services
characteristic: which commercial relation to the consumer is served: selling, advertising, or personalising
positive_test: the work serves a business selling goods or services to consumers
negative_test: recommendation as an output type (Task > Recommendation); consumer behaviour as a discipline (Social & behavioural > Economics or Psychology); the media product itself (Media & entertainment)
examples: E-commerce & pricing; Advertising technology; Demand forecasting
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept on semantics. Four corpus names (advertising 2, Consumer Behavior, Movie Recommendation). Retail and advertising are among the largest industrial ML deployments worldwide; omitting the node because a research institute has no retail partner would encode this institute's 2024 accident into the structure.

name: Telecommunications
characteristic: which part of a carrier network is operated: spectrum and radio link, or network resources
positive_test: the work serves operating a commercial communications network
negative_test: networking research on protocols and architectures (Computing > Computer networks); information theory and coding as machinery (Method); satellite imagery (Modality)
examples: Radio resource management; Channel estimation & signal processing; Network capacity planning
notes: Judgement addition (ISIC J61). Declared homonym with Computing > Computer networks; the split is carrier operations vs networking research, and it will produce annotator disagreement on names like `Wireless Communication`.

name: Application domain not specified
positive_test: the name is on this axis but names no field: `Application-Driven Machine Learning`, `Deep Learning Applications`, `Interdisciplinary Studies`, `Real-world Applications`, `Scientific Machine Learning`
negative_test: any name that identifies a field, however small; contribution-type names such as `Benchmarking`, which are mark_ignore on every axis
notes: Required by AXES.md 8b, which mandates a per-axis uninformative branch but names none for this axis (defect D12). Reported as a line and excluded from this axis's shares.
